paper_lemmas.title: Exact-size normalization and full-square domination
paper_lemmas.conditions: N>=2 for normalized finite-pattern representation; all deterministic finite perturbations of either homogeneous background, translated arbitrarily.
paper_lemmas.statement: tau(N)=normalizedTau(N), where each representative is a side-N finite zero-boundary pattern of exact original distance N. For every pattern g and every common synchronous coin sample, T_sync(g)<=T_sync(full square). Infinite hitting times remain ordered.
paper_lemmas.proof_content_to_explain: Translation and colour complement preserve the product coin law; restricting to the invariant bounding square gives the true finite law; monotonicity uses common fair marks.
paper_lemmas.scope_boundary: The cited profile theorem takes a supremum over exact-N patterns and proves attainment. Do not silently replace the exact-N definition with an arbitrary containing square convention.

paper_lemmas.title: Two-way clock/synchronous comparison with explicit scheduling cost
paper_lemmas.conditions: Finite square internal n>=0 (actual side m=n+2), k>=0 integer; started from full square; actual product clocks and marks.
paper_lemmas.proof_content_to_explain: Common-mark checkerboard splitting; actual monotone censoring; schedule-completion and dependency-rank failure tails. Factor 2 is a union bound over the two checkerboard phases, not independence.

paper_lemmas.title: Weighted slow extinction and its transfer to the original lower bound
paper_lemmas.conditions: Auxiliary half-side L; actual square side 2L+1. Weighted estimate: L>=80, t>=0. Survival half bound: L>=12288000 and t<=L^2/12288000. Synchronous transfer: L>=196608000.
statement: For original N>=786432000 choose L=floor((N-1)/2), fit side 2L+1 inside side N, use r_L>=L^2/393216000 and L>=N/6, then E[T_full_N]>=r_L/4>=N^2/56623104000.
paper_lemmas.proof_content_to_explain: A clipped/frozen protected process and zero-weight forbidden-birth boundary produce the actual weighted mean estimate; loss of protected mass costs at least L^3/128000. The comparison and Markov bound concern real elapsed clock time before the explicit scheduling transfer.
paper_lemmas.scope_boundary: This uses the original frozen lower constant. The later improved lower has its own separate source and validation.

paper_lemmas.title: Mixed-boundary exclusion moments imply local clearing
paper_lemmas.conditions: Auxiliary side M=parameter(L)+2; deterministic monotone initial shape, t>=0; requested southwest side-N block obeys N<=M/8.
statement: For right-half particle count J, Var(J(t))<=M/4. At t_mix=16M^2, E[J]>=M/4.
Monotone-shape geometry: J>=N implies the entire southwest side-N block is white.
Chebyshev then gives P(block not all white at t_mix)<=16/M.
paper_lemmas.proof_content_to_explain: Path exclusion encoding has 2M slots and M particles. Energy derivative is -edgeEnergy, with the exact rate factor already established; Poincare supplies the 4M^2 denominator. Off-diagonal covariance is nonpositive; diagonal Bernoulli variances remain positive.
paper_lemmas.scope_boundary: Auxiliary mixed all-white is not claimed absorbing. This is a fixed-time local-clearing statement, not the original recovery bound.

paper_lemmas.title: Actual cross-size law maps local clearing to the original clock process
paper_lemmas.conditions: Smaller internal n<=m, arbitrary smaller pattern f, larger mixed process initially full; same physical time t and actual retained clocks/marks. For numerical bound, original side N>=16, auxiliary L=4N and M=8N+1.
statement: The site-injection projection of the larger sample has exactly the smaller product law; retaining the ordered event word preserves the update comparison almost surely at every t.
P(original side-N endpoint nonzero at t)<=P(auxiliary southwest side-N block not white at t).
paper_lemmas.proof_content_to_explain: Give the actual injection, retained event sequence and mark pushforward. A drawing should show which local region is controlled and which boundary values dominate.
paper_lemmas.scope_boundary: A heuristic claim that both processes use the same kind of Poisson clocks is insufficient; equality of the projected law and order of retained events are essential.

paper_lemmas.title: Synchronous block success, restart and extended expectation
paper_lemmas.conditions: Original N>=16, k=1296*N^2 schedule layers, b_N=2*128*(k+1)+1=256*(k+1)+1 synchronous rounds.
statement: t_mix=16*(8N+1)^2<=k<=t_k; clock survival is antitone, so C_N(t_k)<=1/8. Scheduling error E_N(k)<=1/8.
The upper half of Lemma 2 yields P_sync(T>b_N)<=1/2.
For every original finite pattern g and integer j>=0, actual independent-future restart gives P(T_g>j*b_N)<=2^(-j).
Extended tail integration yields E[T_g]<=2*b_N. Since b_N<=332033*N^2, E[T_g]<=664066*N^2. Lemma 1 lifts this to the exact-N tau.
paper_lemmas.proof_content_to_explain: Conditional fresh rounds and monotone domination supply a uniform success probability after every surviving block. Infinity is retained until geometric tails force finite mean.
paper_lemmas.scope_boundary: A one-block success probability alone is not an expectation upper bound without the restart connection.
